hero: In a small freestanding hemodialysis unit in Bulacan at dawn, a young Filipino woman intern in a white coat stands at the nurses' station speaking on her phone while a Filipino dialysis nurse in scrubs gestures toward an older man reclined in a dialysis chair; rows of dialysis machines, a wall clock, soft early light through windows, calm but alert mood, no text.

figures.teaches: Each training stage has a different source of authority and a different set of things it may sign, and only the attending carries final responsibility.
figures.content: A vertical ladder with four rungs, bottom to top. Rung 1 'Post-graduate intern': source 'RA 2382 Sec. 11(a): no fee, direct supervision and control of a registered physician'; may 'history, I&O, medicine list, supervised notes, call for help'; may NOT 'prescribe, sign orders, certify forms, cover a unit'. Rung 2 'Resident': source 'PRC license + appointment + privileges'; may 'admit, write orders within privileges, supervise interns'; check 'POD shift only after unit verifies DOH AO 2012-0001 and PSN 2024'. Rung 3 'Nephrology fellow': source 'license + fellowship appointment + procedure privileges'; may 'consults, delegated dialysis orders, teaching'; may NOT 'sign as attending; use the title Fellow of PSN'. Rung 4 'Attending nephrologist': 'final responsibility'. A side rail labeled 'Supervision line' runs from rung 1 to rung 4. Footer: 'Completing a course changes none of these.'

figures.teaches: When a task exceeds your scope, stay at the bedside within scope and escalate down a written list until someone with authority answers.
figures.content: Flowchart. Start box 'Request or patient change beyond your scope'. Two parallel arrows: left 'Stay: assess, monitor, follow unit protocol, basic life support'; right 'Call attending nephrologist (SBAR: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation)'. Decision diamond 'Answer within a few minutes?' Yes -> 'Read back instructions, document time and name'. No -> 'Next name on escalation list: medical director' -> diamond 'Answer?' No -> 'Emergency protocol and transfer to hospital ER'. Red side box 'Stop-and-call triggers: asked to sign/cover beyond status; BP, breathing, consciousness or rhythm change with no qualified physician; no recovery after protocol step; POD absent at shift start'. Footer 'Per unit protocol, but always ask the attending nephrologist for guidance.'
